result.rationale: The diff shows `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod safeParse result object directly (`return refreshTokenResponse;`), and GoogleCalendarService now does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` then `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Previously `key` was `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` — the payload itself. Now the persisted key is the `{ success, data }` wrapper, so subsequent loads reading `credential.key` as google credentials will fail. The mechanism is fully verifiable from the diff.

judged_text: P1 packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` stores the SafeParse result object (`{ success: true, data: ... }`) rather than its `.data`, whereas this field previously stored the credential payload itself. On the first externally synced Google refresh the persisted credential no longer has top-level `refresh_token`/`expiry_date`; the next request fails at `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)`, orphaning every affected existing Google integration until manually reconnected. This survives the happy-path refresh because the in-memory `googleCredentials` still works for that request.
